rationale: bugs_open/315 (now bugs_closed) PLAN decision D8, at the owner's instruction: widen the divergence check's settle window from 30 to 60 minutes. THE WINDOW'S JOB: page_content_divergence (register DGH-015) compares pages.content_hash against the sha256 of the served bytes; the window keeps it off pages whose batched delivery is still in flight. THE EVIDENCE HAS MOVED TWICE, EACH TIME BY AN ORDER OF MAGNITUDE, AND BOTH TIMES I WAS THE ONE WHO OVERSTATED IT. (1) A 2h42m watcher on 2026-08-21 (1,099 re-probes, 85 pages, 95 deploy events) found divergence only at ages 1s/13s/14s, all converged by 156s, and I wrote that 30 minutes was '~128x the largest lag observed'. (2) Re-running the artefact proof after go-live, a random 40-page sample returned 2 DIVERGED aged 15 and 21 MINUTES — max observed 1012s — so the real margin was ~1.8x, not 128x; the watch had sampled only fast deliveries and quoting its maximum as 'the tail' was the error. (3) On 2026-08-22 the check made its first live catch: vetcomparison.uk/index.html served superseded bytes for 9+ HOURS (identical served hash across three passes, no redeploy), and the same page after a byte-identical republish at 08:50Z was still serving the OLD bytes at 09:57Z — age 1h07 — before correcting by 10:20Z. WHAT 60 MINUTES BUYS, HONESTLY: it clears the ~17-minute propagation tail by ~3.5x instead of ~1.8x. WHAT IT DOES NOT BUY: immunity from the 1h07 case, which would still be filed at 60 minutes. WHAT IT COSTS: close to nothing — a real divergence is invisible for its first hour, but detection latency is set by the 4-HOUR discovery rotation, not by this constant, and the motivating case ran 6+ hours.

plan.summary: Change one constant (divergenceSettleWindow 30 -> 60 minutes) in the page_content_divergence discovery check, add a test that pins the literal AND asserts the value reaches the query as $2, and record in the const's own comment that a settle window is structurally the wrong instrument for this (PLAN D9) rather than leaving the number looking authoritative.

edits.rationale: The constant, plus a rewritten evidence block. The comment matters as much as the value here: this number has been wrong by two orders of magnitude twice, and a bare '60 * time.Minute' with a confident comment is how the next reader inherits a third overstatement.
edits.sketch: divergenceSettleWindow = 60 * time.Minute (was 30). The comment now carries ALL THREE measurements in a table rather than only the latest — 1s/13s/14s from the 95-event watch; 15/21 minutes (max 1012s, and NON-MONOTONIC: MATCH @945s, DIVERGED @1012s, MATCH @1079s) from the 40-page sample; and the 2026-08-22 live catch at 9+ hours plus a 1h07 case on the same page after a byte-identical republish. It then states the conclusion those three force: A SETTLE WINDOW CANNOT SEPARATE 'SLOW' FROM 'FAILED' ON THIS ESTATE AND NO VALUE OF THIS CONSTANT WILL, because the observed convergence times (seconds, ~17 min, ~1h20, 9+ hours) OVERLAP the failure they are meant to be distinguished from. Every widening buys false-positive margin and pays in detection latency without resolving the ambiguity. The comment names PLAN D9 (escalate on PERSISTENCE ACROSS PASSES — a page still diverged 4 hours later on a different probe is not in flight; the check already re-detects and the dedup index silently absorbs the repeat) as the real fix, and keeps this constant as an explicitly blunt instrument that is cheap and demonstrably prevents filings (5 in the watch, 2 more in one 40-page sample). Failure mode of being wrong stays bounded in both directions and is stated: a premature finding is FLAG-ONLY (no handler acts) and is RETRACTED on the next pass's positive re-observation. One other comment line updated for consistency so the '5 ways this check could lie' list does not still say 30.

edits.rationale: NEW TEST. Nothing pinned this constant before, so moving a safety threshold traded off against measured behaviour was a one-character change no test would notice.
edits.sketch: Two assertions that a reader might mistake for one. (1) Pins the LITERAL 60 — deliberately NOT `divergenceSettleWindow`, because sizing an assertion from the constant under test is self-referential and cannot fail; that is exactly how this file's per-pass cap test passed against a mutated cap until it was pinned to a literal, which is recorded in its own comment. The failure message tells the author to read the measurements in the const's comment before changing the literal with it. (2) Asserts the value actually REACHES the query as $2, via sqlmock ExpectQuery(...).WithArgs(siteID, float64(3600)) — a const nothing binds is a documented intention, not a behaviour, and the finder is the only place that binds it. BOTH HALVES MUTATION-PROVED, run and restored byte-for-byte: reverting the const to 30 fails the test; swapping the bound value for a fixed 1800 while leaving the const at 60 also fails it. Added to the file's mutation table, which records executed runs rather than intentions.

grounded_in: MEASURED 2026-08-21 10:38-13:20Z: 1,099 re-probes, 85 pages, 95 deploy events; 3 DIVERGED at ages 1s/13s/14s, all converged by 140-156s, 0 of 995 readings at age >= 157s diverged

MEASURED 2026-08-21 19:36Z: a random 40-page sample returned 2 DIVERGED aged 15 and 21 minutes; /model-fine-tuning.html read MATCH @945s, DIVERGED @1012s, MATCH @1079s — non-monotonic, so delivery lands progressively across edge nodes

MEASURED 2026-08-22: first live catch — vetcomparison.uk/index.html served superseded bytes for 9+ hours, identical served hash across three passes (21:53, 01:54, 05:56), deployed_at/updated_at unmoved throughout so no redeploy

MEASURED 2026-08-22: the same page, after a byte-identical republish at 08:50:18Z, recorded served_hash = the OLD bytes at 09:57:37Z (age 1h07) and was correct by 10:20Z — 3/3 fetches from inside the cluster and 10/10 from outside

The const's own prior comment claimed '30 minutes is roughly 128x the largest lag actually observed' — an over-claim from a sample that had caught only fast deliveries, corrected 2026-08-21 and logged in WRONG_CALLS.md

check_page_content_divergence_test.go's per-pass cap test: sizing both fixture and assertion from the const under test made the assertion unfailable until it was pinned to a literal — the precedent this new test follows
PLAN D5's emission rule: flag-only in v1, no handler agent, retraction via CheckResult.Resolved on a positive re-observation — which is what bounds the cost of a premature finding
The discovery rotation's own config: site-discovery-rotation-availability fires every 300s with a 4-hour floor, so detection latency is set by the rotation rather than by this constant
plan.risks: One constant and one new test; no predicate, no emission, no contract, no schema. Inert until the next chassis build and roll — the running v1.0.1323 keeps 30 minutes until then, which is safe because 30 is the value that has been running since 19:23Z on 2026-08-21 and has produced exactly one item, a true positive. THE HONEST CASE AGAINST THIS EDIT, stated because it is real: widening does not fix the ambiguity it is aimed at, and 60 minutes is still inside the range of a legitimately slow delivery (the 1h07 case would still be filed). Anyone reading '60' as 'now safe' would be making the same error I made at '30'. That is why the comment states the structural limit and names D9 rather than presenting the new number as a solution. Second-order risk: a longer window means a page redeployed twice within an hour is judged against the newer stamp only, which is correct but slightly reduces coverage on rapidly-rebuilt pages; the contentIntentUnchanged race guard already discards any candidate whose content_hash or deployed_at moved mid-pass, so this cannot produce a wrong finding, only a skipped one.
